Declare the table, one layer at a time

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_verbs.Rd

Each verb adds a layer to an table_plan(). A later layer wins. The roles — which column goes across, which go down, which carries the row identity — are said once, on table_plan(); these verbs are the things a report really does declare twice. Their arguments are the ones widen_ard() and as_rtftables() already take, so the layering is the only new idea. Nothing runs until the plan is handed to plan_apply() or rtf_tables().

This page is the overview of the verbs, in the order a report is usually written; each has a page of its own. Every verb takes the plan first, as .plan: the pipe passes it by position, and the dot keeps a name in ... such as p (cards' percentage) from being taken for it.

The cells

  • plan_cells(): the cell templates, how each cell is made from the statistics.

  • plan_digits(): the decimals (or significant digits) of the open tokens.

  • plan_stat_groups(): one record's statistics split into named groups.

The rows

  • plan_filter(): drop rows by a condition over their statistics.

  • plan_sort(): the row order, alphabetical or by frequency.

  • plan_levels(): the order of values (and of the analysis variables).

  • plan_labels(): the text values and variables print as.

  • plan_nest(): one variable's rows under one level of another.

  • plan_empty(): what a table with no events says.

More columns

  • plan_total(): a Total column (or row) from the ARD's overall rows.

  • plan_compare(): columns read from comparison records (a p-value, a difference).

The layout

  • plan_stub(): fold the row keys into one row-heading column.

  • plan_row_group(): how a run of rows sharing a value shows.

  • plan_blanks(): where the blank rows go.

  • plan_hide(): columns that do their work without being printed.

  • plan_columns(): widths, decimal alignment and row titles, by name.

  • plan_cell_style(): bold, italic, colour, alignment of cells.

  • plan_style(): the whole table's borders, font and row heights.

The pages

  • plan_paginate_group(): a page per value of a column.

  • plan_paginate_rows(): the row budget, and what a break may cut.

  • plan_paginate_cols(): column blocks, and how the page axes nest.

The header and the text around the table

  • plan_col_header(): the column header and the numbers it prints.

  • plan_titles(): the block of titles above the table.

  • plan_footnotes(): the block of footnotes below the table.

The rest

  • plan_listing(): lay a frame of records out as a listing.

  • plan_append(): another plan's rows under this table's.

  • plan_after(): your own functions, run on the finished pages.

Where each argument goes

Each verb has one job, and its arguments keep the names of the function that does it. This is what each one hands on.

  • plan_cells(..., stats, value, na, notes): how a cell is made. Goes to widen_ard(): cells, stats, value, na, notes; a finished table as_rtftables(): na.

  • plan_digits(..., rounding): the digits. Goes to the open tokens of the templates; on a finished table fmt_numeric().

  • plan_levels(), plan_labels(): the order and text of values. Goes to widen_ard(): levels, labels. A named element of plan_levels() is a value and its text, as base::factor()'s levels and labels (plan_levels(SEX = c(F = "Female", M = "Male")), variable = c(AGE = "Age (years)", "SEX")); plan_labels() names without ordering, and wins value by value over a name plan_levels() gives.

  • plan_total(label, position): a Total column from the ARD's overall rows. Goes to widen_ard(): those rows as one more value of the column key, and its place in levels; the header's {n} there is the study total. plan_levels(.drop_empty = ) leaves out the levels no record has, before the table is made.

  • plan_stat_groups(...): the statistics in named groups. Goes to widen_ard(): stat_groups (the key .stat_group).

  • plan_filter(..., any, parents, by): rows dropped by a condition over the record. Goes to widen_ard(): filter.

  • plan_compare(..., by, position): columns read from comparison records (a test's p-value, a difference and its CI). Goes to widen_ard(): compare.

  • plan_sort(..., stat, keep): the row order. Goes to widen_ard(): sort, sort_stat; a finished table as_rtftables(): sort_by, sort_desc from -name.

  • plan_stub(vars, name, indent, group_summary, before): the row headings. Goes to stub_cols(): vars, label, indent, group_summary.

  • plan_cell_style(cols, header, where, bold, italic, align, color, background, border, underline, indent_twips): how cells look. Goes to style_header(), style_cols(), or rtftable()'s cell_styles for a condition.

  • plan_paginate_group(col, keep, heading, heading_at): a page per value. Goes to as_rtftables(): split = "by_value", group_col; keep = FALSE adds it to drop_cols; heading names each page from a template ({value}, {n}), the name rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) prints; heading_at says where it prints ("section", "title", "none"): the default of rtf_tables(auto_section = , auto_title = ).

  • plan_row_group(mode, collapse, group_col): groups down the body. Goes to as_rtftables(): group_by, collapse_repeats, group_col (a finished table).

  • plan_hide(...): columns not printed. Goes to as_rtftables(): drop_cols.

  • plan_empty(text, when, position, footnote): a table of no events: one row saying so ("No subjects met the criteria."), and a footnote, only when the table has no row or its overall row is 0.

  • plan_blanks(where, first, last, counted): blank rows. Goes to as_rtftables(): blank_rows, blank_row_first, blank_row_end, count_blank_rows; a listing's where = "records" / "none" is listing_spec()'s blank_row = TRUE / FALSE.

  • plan_paginate_rows(max_rows, split, break_before, min_group_rows, cont_label, page_by, heading, heading_at): the row budget, inside the BY pages. Goes to as_rtftables(): max_rows, split, split_rows, min_group_rows, cont_label, page_by; heading and heading_at name each BY page, and say where the name prints, as plan_paginate_group()'s do.

  • plan_paginate_cols(at, cut_by, every, keep, col_header, fit, allow_span_break, order): column blocks. Goes to paginate_cols(), whose arguments have the same names.

  • plan_style(border, ..., border_header, ..., header_bold, ..., table_width_twips, ...): the whole table. Goes to rtftable() / as_rtftables() by the same names; border_* and the default look (header_align, header_bold, header_italic, align, bold, italic, underline) via rtf_table_style().

  • plan_columns(widths, decimal, row_title, auto_width, sep, cell_format, column_widths_twips): the columns. Goes to rtftable(): col_rel_width, row_title, column_widths_twips; set_decimal_split(): cols; as_rtftables(): auto_width, cell_format; widen_ard(): sep.

  • plan_col_header(header, values, header_sep, col_header_align, lines, span): the column header. Goes to set_col_header(): the header (or lines, the header a row at a time) and a data frame of values; a population fills its {n} tokens; as_rtftables(): header_sep; rtftable(): col_header_align.

  • plan_listing(..., type, sep, spacer, spacer_rel_width, layout, wrap, align, record): a listing. Goes to listing_spec(), the same names.

  • plan_titles(), plan_footnotes(): the blocks above and below. Goes to rtf_titles(), rtf_footnotes().

  • plan_after(...): anything else. Goes to your functions of the pages.

plan_columns() declares the columns of this table — widths, alignment, the key separator — and is not rtf_columns(), which addresses the columns of finished pages by their printed names.

Two kinds of names

plan_levels(), plan_labels(), plan_filter(), plan_nest(), plan_stat_groups() and plan_compare() read the normalized ARD's columns (variable, the keys as the ARD names them); plan_hide(), plan_paginate_group(col = ), plan_row_group(), plan_cell_style(), plan_columns() and plan_col_header() read the finished table's columns (the names table_plan(rows = ) gave, row_label, the arms).

The styles plan_cell_style() declares run on the pages in the order written (after the header and the decimal alignment, before any plan_after() step). Its cols may be column names, and .values stands for every value column, so a reordered table keeps them.

See also

table_plan(), plan_apply(), plan_layers()

Examples

# Invented summary statistics of two arms, one row a statistic
st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 4),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "AGE", "SEX", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, NA, "F", "M"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c("continuous", "continuous", "categorical",
                    "categorical"), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "sd", "n", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.2, 9.81, 12, 8, 63.5, 10.2, 9, 11))

# The roles once, then one verb a declaration; plan_apply() runs it
pages <- table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous  = c("Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})"),
             categorical = "{n}") |>
  plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", SEX = "Sex") |>
  plan_stub(name = "Characteristic") |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("Characteristic", "{col}"))) |>
  plan_titles("Table 14.1.1", "Demographics") |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#>               Table 14.1.1               
#>               Demographics               
#> ─────────────────────────────────────────
#> Characteristic    Placebo       Active   
#> ─────────────────────────────────────────
#> Age (years)                              
#>     Mean (SD)   61.2 (9.81)  63.5 (10.20)
#> Sex                                      
#>     F               12            9      
#>     M                8            11     
#> 
#> <rtftable> 5 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Characteristic | Placebo | Active
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     auto / inherited
#>   Titles:     2 line(s)
#>
